title: Physical Activity and Exercise Basics for Adults
content:
Regular physical activity provides extensive systemic health benefits: it strengthens the cardiovascular system, improves insulin sensitivity, supports bone density, enhances mood via neurochemical release, and lowers the risk of chronic illnesses such as type 2 diabetes, stroke, and cardiovascular diseases.

Recommended Physical Activity Guidelines for Adults:
- Aerobic Activity: At least 150 to 300 minutes of moderate-intensity aerobic exercise per week (such as brisk walking at 3-4 mph, cycling on flat terrain, leisurely swimming, or water aerobics), OR 75 to 150 minutes of vigorous-intensity aerobic physical activity (such as running, jogging, lap swimming, or high-intensity interval training), or an equivalent combination.
- Muscle-Strengthening Activity: Engage in resistance exercises targeting all major muscle groups (legs, hips, back, abdomen, chest, shoulders, and arms) at moderate or greater intensity on 2 or more days each week. Examples include bodyweight exercises (pushups, squats), resistance bands, or weight training.
- Balance and Mobility: Older adults should integrate balance training (such as tai chi, heel-to-toe walking) to reduce the risk of fall injuries.

Safe Exercise Practices:
- Warm up for 5 to 10 minutes with light dynamic movement before exercising, and cool down with gentle stretching afterwards.
- Stay well hydrated before, during, and after workouts.
- Listen to your body: mild muscular soreness is normal when starting, but sharp joint pain, sudden dizziness, or chest tightness is not. Individuals with preexisting cardiac conditions should obtain medical clearance before initiating strenuous regimens.
source_name: U.S. Department of Health and Human Services (HHS) & WHO
